_comment: Advise-mode scenarios. expected.decision is the best call; expected.acceptable lists every call that counts as a pass; expected.technology is the card id the call should name ('none' or 'any' when it doesn't matter). A scenario whose acceptable list lacks USE IT counts toward the Unnecessary rUv Recommendation Rate. Expectations follow references/decision-policy.md and the 2026-10-07 snapshot; when a card's maturity changes, revisit the scenarios that cite it. Ruflo scenarios follow the native-first rule (decision-policy.md section 5): parallelism or repetition alone is not a Ruflo fit.

scenarios.prompt: Every Monday I research 40 competitor companies, identify product changes, compare their messaging and write competitive briefs. It takes most of the day in a single Claude Code session. Is this a Ruflo thing?
scenarios.notes: PRD example 28, recalibrated native-first (2026-10-07): built-in subagents plus a skill already give the parallelism and repetition.

scenarios.prompt: We're a 3-person agency. Every Monday we run the same competitor-research crew for 8 clients, built with Claude Code subagents and a skill. But the agents can't see what each other or last week's run found, so they re-research the same things; each of us runs it slightly differently; and our token bill doubled with no idea which step is eating it. It's internal and we're fine with fast-moving tools. Is this where Ruflo comes in?
scenarios.notes: Stacked needs native doesn't cover: shared memory across runs, one workflow for a team, per-step cost tracking.

scenarios.prompt: I run big parallel refactors across our TypeScript monorepo: 20 to 30 agents working on independent packages at once. With Claude Code's built-in subagents they keep editing the same shared files and overwriting each other, and decisions made in one session are lost by the next. Internal tooling, and I'm comfortable with fast-moving tools. Would Ruflo fix this?
scenarios.notes: Worktree isolation plus a shared decision record: a current pain native subagents hit.

scenarios.prompt: I want to learn multi-agent orchestration hands-on. I have a scratch folder just for experiments and nothing depends on it. What's the gentlest way to try Ruflo?
scenarios.notes: Learning goal, sandbox: USE IT for the sandbox via the plugin path, not a full init.

scenarios.prompt: Each month I do due diligence on 25 startups in a fund's pipeline: market research, a competitor scan, founder background and a risk memo for each. The startups are independent. I work in Claude Code. Is it worth bringing in Ruflo?
scenarios.notes: Parallel, independent, monthly: native subagents and a skill cover it.

scenarios.prompt: I run a grant-writing consultancy. Every proposal needs a funder-requirements analysis, a budget check, the writing, and a compliance review. I do about 10 proposals a month in Claude Code and we keep missing funder requirements. Could a rUv tool help?
scenarios.notes: A requirements-checker subagent addresses the pain natively.

scenarios.prompt: We already use Ruflo's swarm and workflow plugins for our weekly research crew and they work well. Our token bill has doubled in two months and we can't tell which agents or steps are responsible. Is there something in Ruflo for that, or should we look elsewhere?
scenarios.notes: Already on Ruflo; one more plugin (cost tracker) fixes a current pain.

scenarios.prompt: We're building an Electron desktop app for field geologists: semantic search over about 200,000 PDF field notes. It must work fully offline on laptops at remote sites, and the data can't go to any cloud. We're a Node/TypeScript team, it's our own product, and we can live with a pre-1.0 dependency if it sits behind an interface. Should we look at RuVector?
scenarios.notes: Offline, local, privacy, Node, large index, adapter accepted.

scenarios.prompt: I'm prototyping a coding agent that should get better from test results across thousands of runs, Reflexion-style: record what it tried, whether the tests passed, and a critique, then reuse the lessons. It's a sandbox repo, TypeScript, nothing depends on it, and alpha software is fine. Is AgentDB worth trying for the memory?
scenarios.notes: Recalibrated 2026-10-07: AgentDB is alpha with a feedback bug, so its honest USE IT today is a sandbox experiment with a real feedback signal (tests) and volume. The earlier client-conventions case is better served by a markdown file.

scenarios.prompt: I maintain agent setups for 8 client repos. Each client wants a versioned, signed agent package they own, working in Claude Code and Codex. Right now I hand-copy CLAUDE.md files and skills between repos. Is there a rUv tool for this?
scenarios.notes: Shipping signed, versioned harnesses to clients; pre-1.0 so CONSIDER LATER is defensible.

scenarios.prompt: Our university lab is doing an occupancy-sensing research project. Cameras are banned in the building for privacy reasons. We have some ESP32-S3 boards and it's a proof of concept. Anything in the rUv world for this?
scenarios.notes: Camera-free sensing, research, hardware on hand.

scenarios.prompt: Compare pgvector and RuVector for our knowledge base. It's about 2,000 support articles in Postgres with pgvector, and search works fine. Should we switch?
scenarios.notes: PRD 4.2: boring wins.

scenarios.prompt: We have a SaaS that drafts replies to customer reviews for business owners to approve. Next quarter we plan to add a brand-policy checker, a legal-risk checker and an escalation step. Should we be planning around rUv tech?
scenarios.notes: Runtime is a web app; multi-step checks are future; Ruflo is a coding-assistant add-on.

scenarios.prompt: I'm a solo founder. One Claude Code session does my weekly reporting across 3 data sources and it's fine. I might have 20 clients next year. Should I set up Ruflo now?
scenarios.notes: Future scale is a trigger, not a reason.

scenarios.prompt: Our notes app does semantic search with Supabase pgvector. Customers have asked for an offline mode, and it's on next year's roadmap. Does RuVector matter for us?
scenarios.notes: Offline is a future requirement: a clean trigger.

scenarios.prompt: Our support-agent prototype stores conversation history in Postgres. Product wants it to 'learn from resolved tickets' eventually, but we don't have any feedback labels yet. Do we need AgentDB?
scenarios.notes: No feedback signal yet; plain tables first.

scenarios.prompt: We ship an AI agent to enterprise customers on-prem. Auditors might one day ask for a tamper-evident record of what knowledge the agent had. It isn't required yet. Should we adopt RVF?
scenarios.notes: Future requirement; RVF is a research draft.

scenarios.prompt: I'm one developer with one repo, but someday I might package my Claude Code setup and sell it to other developers. Should I use MetaHarness now?
scenarios.notes: Distribution is hypothetical.

scenarios.prompt: I'm making a SaaS that takes customer reviews, drafts replies and lets business owners approve them. Should I be using any of the rUv stuff?
scenarios.notes: PRD example 27.

scenarios.prompt: I'm building a simple Astro marketing site with a contact form, and I want a chatbot that answers questions from our 30 FAQ entries. Does any rUv technology belong here?
scenarios.notes: 30 entries fit in a prompt.

scenarios.prompt: I need to generate product descriptions for the 200 products in my Shopify store, once. Should I use Ruflo swarms for this?
scenarios.notes: One-off batch; a loop over one model call.

scenarios.prompt: There's a bug in my React app's date picker: it shows the wrong day in some time zones. Should I use Ruflo to fix it?
scenarios.notes: Ruflo's own skill file says not for simple bug fixes.

scenarios.prompt: I'm building a personal habit-tracker iOS app with SwiftUI and CloudKit. Is there anything from the rUv ecosystem I should use?
scenarios.notes: No agent, memory or search problem.

scenarios.prompt: We need an internal admin panel in Rails for 10 employees to manage orders. Would rUv tech make it better?
scenarios.notes: CRUD.

scenarios.prompt: I want a daily digest of my Gmail summarised by one model call each morning. Do I need agents or memory from the rUv stack?
scenarios.notes: One scheduled call.

scenarios.prompt: We have a nightly Python ETL from Stripe into BigQuery. We want to add an LLM step that labels refund reasons. Any rUv tools worth adding?
scenarios.notes: Python; one classification call per row.

scenarios.prompt: I'm building a Chrome extension that rewrites selected text in a friendlier tone. Should it use anything from rUv?
scenarios.notes: One call.

scenarios.prompt: I'm building a restaurant booking website for a client, with SMS confirmations through Twilio. Is there a place for rUv technology?
scenarios.notes: No AI requirement at all.

scenarios.prompt: RuVector is written in Rust and way faster. Should I replace pgvector in our Supabase app? We have 50,000 rows, search p95 is 40 ms, and users are happy.
scenarios.notes: Rust-is-faster trap; no current pain.

scenarios.prompt: I watched a video about agent swarms. I write one blog post a week. Should my blog-writing setup use eight agents?
scenarios.notes: Swarm FOMO.

scenarios.prompt: Should I run ruflo init in all 12 of my client project repos so my setup is more advanced? Nothing specific is broken, I just want to be ahead of the curve.
scenarios.notes: VERY HIGH, client repos, no requirement; init edits global CLAUDE.md by default.

scenarios.prompt: AgentDB says it's 150x faster than SQLite. My app keeps 5,000 rows of notes in SQLite. Should I move to AgentDB?
scenarios.notes: Benchmark trap; alpha; small data.

scenarios.prompt: I'm building a browser extension that does semantic search over a user's saved bookmarks entirely client-side, because privacy is the selling point. Users have around 2,000 bookmarks. Should I use RuVector's WASM build?
scenarios.notes: Local is real, but 2,000 items is brute-force territory.

scenarios.prompt: I want 'self-learning' agents for my landing-page copy generator. I make about 10 pages a month and I have no conversion data hooked up. Which rUv memory tool should I use?
scenarios.notes: No feedback signal, tiny volume.

scenarios.prompt: Should I use RVF to make my chatbot's memory portable? I really just want a backup of the conversation history.
scenarios.notes: Portable just means exportable.

scenarios.prompt: Our medical clinic wants to monitor patients' breathing in the waiting room without cameras. Can we deploy RuView for that in production?
scenarios.notes: Medical and production; the project says not a medical device.

scenarios.prompt: We're a 3-person agency doing SEO audits for about 15 clients a month. Each audit is a crawl, a content review, a technical review and a report, and right now one person does each audit in Claude Code. Would Ruflo help?
scenarios.notes: Native-first: repeating, partly parallel work that subagents and a shared skill cover.

scenarios.prompt: Our developer docs site has 40,000 pages and uses Algolia keyword search. Product wants search by meaning. We're on Next.js with Postgres on Neon. Should we use RuVector?
scenarios.notes: pgvector on Neon is the boring answer.

scenarios.prompt: I'm researching a book and have 3,000 PDFs of interviews. I want semantic search on my laptop with no cloud. I'm not a developer, but I can run npx commands. Is RuVector the answer?
scenarios.notes: Non-developer; a pre-1.0 library needs code; existing local apps are the boring answer.

scenarios.prompt: I already ran Ruflo's full init in my main repo, and separately I use pgvector for my app's search. Are these overlapping? Should I add AgentDB too?
scenarios.notes: Ruflo memory already runs on AgentDB; pgvector serves the app. Overlap check.
